narrative.title: Every Flight Roster the Charter Could Fly
narrative.scenario: A charter operator lists candidate crew members and must file every possible roster — including the empty one — before the season starts. Each crew member is either on a roster or not, so the planner walks the list once and forks at every name: file the rosters that include this member, then the ones that don't. With all-distinct candidates, no two rosters coincide.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n distinct integers.
narrative.outputFormat: All 2^n subsets, in the order the include-first depth-first walk emits them.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n * 2^n) — 2^n subsets, each copied in O(n)
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: The include-first walk at index 0 emits every roster containing 1 before the rosters built from the rest; the empty roster lands last.
One member: take them, or file the empty roster.

hintLevels: Level 1: Each element has a binary fate — in or out — so the answer space is a binary tree of depth n.
Level 2: Recurse on the index: push the element, recurse (include), pop it, recurse again (exclude); record the subset whenever the index runs past the end.
Level 3: The base case fires at index == n, so every leaf records exactly one subset and no dedup logic is needed while elements stay distinct.
